tagline: Indonesian wastra, shaped for contemporary life.
eyebrow: Tangerang Selatan · Indonesian woven fashion & craft

story.title: From Balige weaving to a wider Indonesian fashion story.
story.body: Founded by Ida R. Tampubolon, Li-Uli grew from a craft idea rooted in Balige into an Indonesian wastra fashion brand. Early products paired laminated burlap with Tenun Balige and Ulos Batak for bags and wallets; the brand has since expanded into broader fashion pieces while carrying traditional woven textiles into contemporary design and international-facing showcases.

stats.label: registered and sold from Tangerang Selatan

highlights.title: Wastra as the identity
highlights.body: Tenun Balige, Ulos Batak and other Indonesian woven traditions form the visual language behind Li-Uli products.

highlights.title: Material with a story
highlights.body: The brand’s early bags combine laminated burlap with woven textile accents, using a simple material base to foreground regional craft.

highlights.title: Craft with social impact
highlights.body: Ida Tampubolon has trained people with disabilities in Toba to improve bag design and develop fashion products from local wastra through the Rumah BUMN INALUM Toba ecosystem.

highlights.title: Beyond the local market
highlights.body: Li-Uli has been promoted in international-facing programs; Tangsel’s Dekranasda has also cited the brand’s woven bags in connection with recurring orders from a Japanese company.
